column3: to rush; to rinse; to brew (with hot water)
column4: 孩子们一下课就冲出了教室。
column5: As soon as class ended, the children rushed out of the classroom.
column6: 冲 is read chōng for "rush", "rinse" and "brew". It is read chòng in 冲着 (facing, aimed at).

column4: 手机没电了，我要充电。
column5: My phone has no battery left; I need to charge it.
column6: 充电 is a verb plus object, so it splits: 充了电, 充满电 (fully charged).

column4: 你要做好充分的准备。
column5: You must make full preparations.
column6: 充分 describes abstract things such as preparation, reasons or use. It can also come before a verb: 充分利用 (to make full use of).

column3: to be full of; to fill with
column4: 他的心里充满了快乐。
column5: His heart is full of joy.
column6: 充满 is followed by a feeling or an abstract thing (充满希望). For a container that is full, say 满.

column3: to top up (money on a card or account)
column4: 你的卡里没有钱了，要去充值。
column5: There is no money left on your card; you need to go and top it up.
column6: 充值 is to add money to a card, a phone account or an app.

column4: 植物需要充足的阳光和水。
column5: Plants need sufficient sunlight and water.
column6: 充足 describes something there is enough of: 阳光充足, 时间充足, 睡眠充足.

column4: 老师请他重复了一遍。
column5: The teacher asked him to repeat it once.
column6: 重 is read chóng in 重复 and 重新 (again). It is read zhòng in 重要 and 很重 (heavy).

column4: 我的苹果里有一条小虫子。
column5: There is a little worm in my apple.
column6: 虫子 is the everyday word for a small crawling or flying creature. Worms are counted with 条, other bugs with 只.

column4: 我家有两只宠物，一只猫和一只狗。
column5: My home has two pets, a cat and a dog.
column6: 宠物 is an animal kept as a pet. Pets are counted with 只 (or 条 for fish and snakes).

column3: to pull out; to draw; to smoke
column4: 他从书包里抽出了一本书。
column5: He pulled a book out of his school bag.
column6: 抽 means to pull something out of a group or a container. It also means to smoke (抽烟) and to find a moment (抽空).

column4: 小狗长得很丑，可是我很喜欢它。
column5: The puppy is very ugly, but I like it very much.
column6: 丑 is a strong word. It is better not to say a person is 丑 to their face. Its opposite is 漂亮 or 美.

column4: 你的鞋很臭，别放在房间里。
column5: Your shoes smell bad; do not leave them in the room.
column6: 臭 is read chòu and means a bad smell. Its opposite is 香 (fragrant).

column3: beginning; first; at the start of
column4: 他是月初来的。
column5: He came at the beginning of the month.
column6: 初 marks the start of a period: 月初, 年初. It is also a prefix in 初中 (junior high school) and in 初一 (the first day of a lunar month).

column4: 这本书是去年出版的。
column5: This book was published last year.
column6: 出版 is for books, magazines and music. A publishing house is 出版社.

column4: 我在上初级汉语班。
column5: I am in an elementary Chinese class.
column6: 初级 is the first of three steps: 初级, 中级, 高级 (beginner, intermediate, advanced). It comes before a noun.

column4: 学习汉语的初期，大家都觉得很难。
column5: In the early stage of learning Chinese, everyone finds it hard.
column6: 初期 is the first part of a process. Its opposite is 后期 (the late stage).

column4: 她的表现很出色。
column5: Her performance is outstanding.
column6: 出色 praises someone's performance, work or result: 工作出色, 表现出色.

column3: to sell; to put on sale
column4: 这套房子正在出售。
column5: This flat is being sold.
column6: 出售 is a formal word for 卖. A sign that says 出售 means "for sale".

column3: to attend (a meeting or an event)
column4: 经理会出席明天的会议。
column5: The manager will attend tomorrow's meeting.
column6: 出席 is for formal meetings and events. 参加 is the general word for taking part.

column3: to come from; to originate from
column4: 这个句子出自一本老书。
column5: This sentence comes from an old book.
column6: 出自 gives the source of a saying, a work or an idea: 出自一本书, 出自一位画家.

column4: 除夕晚上，一家人一起吃饭。
column5: On the evening of New Year's Eve, the whole family eats together.
column6: 除夕 is the night before Chinese New Year. Families gather for a big dinner.

column3: to be in (a place or a state); to get along
column4: 这个村子处在两座山中间。
column5: This village lies between two mountains.
column6: 处 is read chǔ as a verb: 处在, 相处. As a noun (a place, a point) it is read chù, as in 好处 (benefit) and 到处 (everywhere).

column3: to deal with; to handle; to dispose of
column4: 这件事我来处理。
column5: I will deal with this matter.
column6: 处理 also means to get rid of things (处理旧东西) or to sell goods cheaply (处理价).

column3: to be in (a state or position)
column4: 他现在处于危险之中。
column5: He is now in danger.
column6: 处于 is followed by a state or position: 处于困难中, 处于中间. It is formal.

column3: to pass on; to spread; to hand down
column4: 请把这封信传给他。
column5: Please pass this letter on to him.
column6: 传 is read chuán here. In the sense of a biography it is read zhuàn.

column4: 这个消息传播得很快。
column5: This news spreads very fast.
column6: 传播 is to spread to many people: news, ideas, culture or a disease.

column4: 请把这个消息传递给大家。
column5: Please pass this news on to everyone.
column6: 传递 is to hand something from one person to the next: a message, a book, a feeling.

column4: 这座山有一个有名的传说。
column5: This mountain has a famous legend.
column6: 传说 is also a verb: 传说这里有一条河 means "it is said that there is a river here".

column4: 过年是中国最重要的传统节日。
column5: Chinese New Year is China's most important traditional festival.
column6: 传统 is a noun (a tradition) and an adjective before a noun (传统文化, 传统节日).

column4: 窗台上放着一杯水。
column5: A glass of water is placed on the windowsill.
column6: 窗台 is the flat part under a window. 台 is read tái.

column4: 我每个星期洗一次床单。
column5: I wash the bed sheet once a week.
column6: 床单 is the sheet on a bed. Its measure word is 条 or 张.

column4: 这家公司很重视创新。
column5: This company puts great value on innovation.
column6: 创新 is both a verb and a noun. It means to bring in something new, not just to copy.

column4: 他毕业以后自己创业了。
column5: After graduating he started his own business.
column6: 创业 is to build a new company or career from the start. It is a verb plus object.

column4: 他创造了一个新的游戏。
column5: He created a new game.
column6: 创造 makes something that did not exist before. It also goes with abstract things: 创造机会, 创造条件.

column3: to create (a work of art or writing)
column4: 他正在创作一首新歌。
column5: He is creating a new song.
column6: 创作 is for art, music and writing. As a noun it is the work itself. 创造 can be used for anything new.

column4: 我想学更多的汉语词汇。
column5: I want to learn more Chinese vocabulary.
column6: 词汇 is all the words of a language or all the words a person knows. A single word is 词 or 单词.

column3: to resign; to quit a job
column4: 他对工作不满意，所以辞职了。
column5: He was not happy with his job, so he resigned.
column6: 辞职 is a verb plus object: 辞了职, 想辞职. It is the normal word for leaving a job by your own choice.

column4: 他三年前去了国外，此后再也没有回来过。
column5: He went abroad three years ago and has not come back since.
column6: 此后 is formal. It looks forward from a moment already mentioned. Its opposite is 此前.

column4: 此前我从来没有听过这个名字。
column5: Before this I had never heard this name.
column6: 此前 is a formal way to say "before this point". Its opposite is 此后.

column3: at this moment; at that time
column4: 此时此刻，我只想回家。
column5: At this very moment, all I want is to go home.
column6: 此时 is a formal way to say 这个时候. 此时此刻 means "at this very moment".

column4: 这个电影很刺激，我看得很紧张。
column5: This film is very exciting, and I feel nervous when I watch it.
column6: 刺激 is a verb (to stimulate, to upset someone) and a noun (a stimulus). In speech 很刺激 means "thrilling".

column4: 他从不迟到。
column5: He is never late.
column6: 从不 means "never" as a habit: 从不 + verb. It is the short form of 从来不.

column4: 他每天锻炼，从而身体越来越好。
column5: He exercises every day, and thus his health gets better and better.
column6: 从而 introduces the result or aim that follows from the first part. It is written style and comes in the second clause.

column3: in the past; once upon a time
column4: 从前有一个小村子，村子里有很多树。
column5: Once upon a time there was a small village with many trees.
column6: 从前 is like 以前 but sounds more like a story. 从前 + 有 begins a tale.

column3: to be engaged in; to work in
column4: 他从事教育工作已经十年了。
column5: He has been working in education for ten years.
column6: 从事 is followed by a line of work or an activity: 从事教育, 从事研究. It is formal.

column4: 运动可以促进身体健康。
column5: Exercise can promote good health.
column6: 促进 helps something develop or improve: 促进发展, 促进了解.

column3: to urge; to push; to cause (someone to do)
column4: 这件事促使他改变了想法。
column5: This event pushed him to change his mind.
column6: 促使 follows a cause: A 促使 B + verb means "A causes B to do something".

column4: 商店正在促销，很多东西都很便宜。
column5: The shop is having a sales promotion, and many things are very cheap.
column6: 促销 is a business word for special offers to sell more. 促销活动 is a sales promotion.

column4: 妈妈一直催我快一点起床。
column5: Mum keeps urging me to get up quickly.
column6: 催 means to press someone to hurry up: 催他, 催我们.

column3: to store; to keep (in a place)
column4: 请把你的包存放在这里。
column5: Please store your bag here.
column6: 存放 is to put things in a place for safe keeping, such as a locker or a box.

column4: 我在银行里有一点儿存款。
column5: I have a little savings in the bank.
column6: 存款 is money kept in a bank. As a verb it means to deposit: 去银行存款.

column4: 这个问题现在还存在。
column5: This problem still exists now.
column6: 存在 is for problems, differences and ideas. For "there is a thing", use 有.

column4: 学校采取了新的安全措施。
column5: The school has adopted new safety measures.
column6: 措施 is a step taken to deal with a problem. It goes with 采取: 采取措施.

column4: 两个人终于达成了一致。
column5: The two people finally reached an agreement.
column6: 达成 goes with an agreement made by talking: 达成一致 (reach agreement), 达成协议.

column3: to dress up; to make oneself up
column4: 她今天打扮得很漂亮。
column5: She is dressed up beautifully today.
column6: 打扮 is to make yourself look good with clothes and make-up. 打扮得 + adjective tells how.

column3: to pack; to pack up leftovers to take away
column4: 我们吃不完这些菜，请帮我打包。
column5: We cannot finish these dishes; please pack them up for me to take away.
column6: 打包 also means to pack things into boxes or bags, for example before you move house.

column4: 请不要打断别人说话。
column5: Please do not interrupt other people when they speak.
column6: 打断 is to break into someone's speech or work. Say 打断他, or 打断他的话.

column4: 他不小心打破了一个杯子。
column5: He accidentally broke a cup.
column6: 打破 is to break something with force. It also works for things that are not physical: 打破沉默 (to break the silence).

column4: 我想向你打听一个人。
column5: I would like to ask you about someone.
column6: 打听 is to ask around to find something out, such as news about a person or a place. 听 is neutral here: dǎting.

column4: 这个孩子很大胆，一个人去了山里。
column5: This child is very bold and went into the mountains alone.
column6: 大胆 can be praise ("brave") or a warning ("too daring"). Its opposite is 胆小 (timid).

column4: 这里的人大多喜欢喝茶。
column5: Most people here like drinking tea.
column6: 大多 comes before the verb: 大多是, 大多喜欢. 大多数 is a noun, "the majority".

column4: 明天学校要开大会。
column5: The school will hold a big meeting tomorrow.
column6: 大会 is a meeting of many people. You say 开大会 to hold one.

column4: 政府大力发展旅游。
column5: The government is vigorously developing tourism.
column6: 大力 is an adverb before a verb: 大力发展, 大力支持 (to give strong support).

column4: 那位大妈在公园里跳舞。
column5: That auntie is dancing in the park.
column6: 大妈 is a friendly way to call a woman about your mother's age or older, even a stranger. The man's form is 大爷.

column4: 我去超市买了一些大米。
column5: I went to the supermarket and bought some rice.
column6: 大米 is the raw rice. Cooked rice is 米饭.

column4: 睡觉对大脑很重要。
column5: Sleep is very important for the brain.
column6: 大脑 is the brain as the organ of thinking.

column3: a large batch of; large numbers of
column4: 公司买了大批新电脑。
column5: The company bought a large number of new computers.
column6: 大批 comes before a noun for goods or people: 大批游客 (large numbers of tourists).

column4: 那座大厦很高，里面有很多公司。
column5: That building is very tall, and there are many companies in it.
column6: 大厦 is a large tall building, often for offices. Its name often ends in 大厦.

column4: 结婚是人生的大事。
column5: Getting married is a major event in life.
column6: 大事 is an important matter. Its opposite is 小事 (a trifle).

column4: 动物园里有两头大象。
column5: There are two elephants in the zoo.
column6: 大象 is counted with 头. The short form 象 is used in compounds.

column4: 这个城市今年有一个大型活动。
column5: This city has a large-scale event this year.
column6: 大型 comes before a noun: 大型活动, 大型商场. Its opposite is 小型.

column4: 那位大爷每天早上都在公园里锻炼。
column5: That old gentleman exercises in the park every morning.
column6: 大爷 is a friendly way to call a man about your father's age or older. 爷 is neutral: dàye. When it means your father's elder brother it is read dà yé.

column4: 十大于九。
column5: Ten is greater than nine.
column6: 大于 is used in maths and measuring: A 大于 B means A > B. 小于 means "less than".

column4: 这种音乐很受大众欢迎。
column5: This kind of music is very popular with the public.
column6: 大众 is ordinary people in general. 受大众喜欢 means "to be popular with the public".

column4: 我想代他向你问好。
column5: I would like to say hello to you on his behalf.
column6: 代 means "to act in place of" (代他), "a generation" (年轻的一代) and "an age" (古代).

column4: 你代表我们班去开会。
column5: You will represent our class at the meeting.
column6: 代表 is a person (a representative) or a verb. As a verb it also means "to stand for": 红色代表好运.
